obligation: HIPAA breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI (presumed unless the 164.402 four-factor assessment shows a low probability of compromise). Clock starts at discovery: the first day known, or by reasonable diligence would have been known, to any workforce member (164.404(a)(2))
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Each affected individual by first-class mail (or email if the individual agreed); substitute notice if contact information is out of date
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - covered entity

obligation: HIPAA breach notice to HHS (500 or more)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals (likely here: the delivery log exports in the shared drive name several thousand patients)
deadline: Contemporaneously with the individual notices (within 60 days of discovery)
notify: HHS Secretary through the OCR breach portal
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more

obligation: HIPAA breach log to HHS (fewer than 500)
trigger: Breach affecting fewer than 500 individuals (for example, only the ALF medication lists)
deadline: No later than 60 days after the end of the calendar year in which the breach was discovered
notify: HHS Secretary through the OCR breach portal
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if fewer than 500

obligation: HIPAA media notice
trigger: Breach affecting more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Prominent media outlets serving Florida (or the affected area)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 500 Florida residents

obligation: Law enforcement delay (HIPAA)
trigger: A law enforcement official states that notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: Delay for the period in a written statement; if oral, document it and delay no longer than 30 days unless a written statement follows
notify: Hold HIPAA notices; document the request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Business associate breach notice to the pharmacy (inbound; MSP and SaaS vendors)
trigger: A business associate (MSP, PMS vendor, cloud fax vendor, productivity suite vendor) discovers a breach of the pharmacy's unsecured PHI
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after the business associate's discovery (BAAs may set shorter periods)
notify: The pharmacy (Store Manager as Privacy Officer)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in each BAA

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (includes medical history, treatment, or diagnosis and health insurance identifiers). Clock starts at determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination. Notice under the HIPAA rules is deemed compliant with this subsection if the pharmacy notifies individuals under those rules (501.171(4)(g))
notify: Affected Florida residents
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - plan to the 30-day date; counsel confirms the deemed-compliance path

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals). A pharmacy that timely sends the Department a copy of its HIPAA notice is deemed compliant with subsection (3)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

obligation: Florida law enforcement delay
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines individual notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay on the agency's written request for the period it specifies
notify: Hold Florida individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the pharmacy (inbound; MSP, backup service, and SaaS vendors)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a third-party agent
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the agent's determination
notify: The pharmacy (Store Manager)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - add to the MSP contract and BAAs at renewal

obligation: Other states' breach laws
trigger: Affected patients who reside outside Florida (for example seasonal residents)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check residency of affected patients

obligation: DEA report of an EPCS security incident
trigger: The pharmacy determines that an auditable event, or the attack, compromised or could have compromised the integrity of controlled substance prescription records (for example, attacker use of a PMS session or credential)
deadline: Within one business day of the determination
notify: The PMS vendor (application service provider) and DEA (local Diversion field office; counsel confirms the channel)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - decide on day 0 to 1 with the PMS vendor's audit trail review

obligation: Stop processing EPCS when the application is non-compliant
trigger: The PMS vendor notifies the pharmacy that the application no longer meets the EPCS rule or has a non-compliance issue
deadline: Immediately; resume only after the vendor confirms compliance and updates are installed
notify: No outside notice; record the stop and restart in the incident log
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - ask the vendor directly whether the PMS remains compliant after the incident

obligation: CSOS private key loss or compromise
trigger: Loss, theft, or compromise of the CSOS private key or its password is substantiated (for example, malware on the owner laptop)
deadline: Within 24 hours of substantiation, by a revocation request
notify: DEA CSOS certification authority
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the owner laptop is affected; apply for a new certificate afterward (1311.25)

obligation: Theft or significant loss of controlled substances (DEA)
trigger: Discovery of a theft or significant loss of controlled substances (for example, a break-in during the outage or a count shortage)
deadline: In writing within one business day of discovery; DEA Form 106 within 45 days after discovery
notify: DEA Field Division Office; Form 106 through DEA's Diversion Control Division secure network application
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a theft or significant loss occurs

obligation: Theft or significant loss of controlled substances (Florida)
trigger: Discovery of a theft or significant loss of controlled substances
deadline: Within 24 hours after discovery
notify: Sheriff of the county
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a theft or significant loss occurs

obligation: PDMP reporting during downtime
trigger: Each controlled substance dispensed in Florida, including on paper during an outage
deadline: As soon as possible but no later than the close of the next business day after dispensing, unless the department approves an extension or exemption
notify: Florida PDMP (Department of Health)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - enter paper-log dispensings through the PDMP web portal from a clean device, or ask for an extension before the deadline

obligation: PDMP consultation not possible during an outage
trigger: The PDMP cannot be consulted because of a temporary technological or electrical failure
deadline: At the time of dispensing
notify: No outside notice; document the reason in the prescription record and dispense no more than a 3-day supply
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - on the downtime card

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement (FBI) or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI through IC3 or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
citation: Voluntary (no statutory deadline for this pharmacy)
trigger: Ransomware or other significant cyber incident
deadline: As soon as practical (day 0 to 2), before any ransom decision
notify: FBI (IC3 online report); CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - recommended

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident, extortion demand, or data theft
deadline: Per policy: prompt notice through the 24x7 breach hotline, before hiring outside firms; use panel counsel and forensics
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: ALF management company notice
citation: Supply agreement with the ALF management company (contract)
trigger: Incident affecting ALF residents' data or delaying adherence packs
deadline: Per the agreement; call each ALF director of nursing on day 0 about pack changes
notify: ALF management company; each ALF director of nursing
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: PBM network agreement notices
trigger: Data security incident or inability to submit claims
deadline: Per each agreement
notify: Each PBM's network contact
applies_at_this_tier: Check each agreement; not a legal duty under federal or Florida law

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (voluntary until then); as proposed, an SBA-small pharmacy outside the health care sector criteria would not be covered. Recheck when final

obligation: Part 2 record breach
trigger: Breach of SUD treatment records from a Part 2 program
deadline: Same as HIPAA: no later than 60 days after discovery
notify: Patients, HHS, and media
applies_at_this_tier: No - the pharmacy is not a Part 2 program (42 CFR 2.11)

obligation: FTC Health Breach Notification Rule
trigger: Breach by a vendor of personal health records not covered by HIPAA
deadline: Individuals and media: within 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Individuals, FTC, media
applies_at_this_tier: No - the rule does not apply to HIPAA covered entities (16 CFR 318.1)

obligation: Covered telecommunications / Kaspersky article discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the pharmacy holds no federal contracts
